statins have a cholesterol-independent vasoprotection that is mediated, in part by inhibition of small GTPases Rho and Rac.

statins have cholesterol-independent vasoprotection effects mediated by the inhibition of Rho and/or Rac small G-proteines, which results in nitric oxide synthetase upregulation, superoxide reduction and endothelium function improvement.
statins exert vasoprotective actions by modulating the activity of small GTPases Rho and Rac, which are important for nitric oxide bioactivity and superoxide generation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the effects of statins on endothelial function and their signaling mechanisms.

the role of Rho and its effectors, ROCK and Rho kinase, in the regulation of vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation and endothelial nitric-oxide synthase expression and the effects of statins in these processes.
elucidation of the mechanisms of endothelium-dependent and independent vasoprotection of statins, and their clinical implications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
statin therapy improves the endothelial function, which may be related to their ability to inhibit small GTPases Rho and Rac, and that this effect is independent of cholesterol lowering.
statins have beneficial effects on endothelial dysfunction and that these effects are mediated by inhibition of Rho/Rac GTPase activity.
statins are not only cholesterol lowering but also have a beneficial impact on the vasculature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
statins have a pleiotropic effect that is mediated, in part through the inhibition of Rho and the activation of Rac, which results in endothelial dysfunction.
statin therapy may improve endothelial function by inhibiting Rho and Rac activity, which in turn may improve nitric oxide bioactivity and decrease superoxide production.
statin treatment may be beneficial for patients with endothelial dysfunction, whereas statin discontinuation may have deleterious effects on endothelial function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
statins may have beneficial effects on endothelium and vasculature through the inhibition of Rho and/or Rac.
statins exert cholesterol-independent effects on endothelium and signaling mechanisms that may be relevant to the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
statins exert cholesterol-independent effects that may be important for the prevention of cardiovascular events.
